event: VXE-808 aborted its VTOL launch at about 150 ft when the GCS battery balance indicator turned red, and descended to a harder than normal landing that compressed the landing pad.
failure_mode: HLB cell voltage imbalance (cell sag) under launch load, flagged by the battery balance indicator, causing an automatic launch abort
contributing: Fleet-wide HLB cell dropout problem tracked in VXEP-1449 (electrolyte loss in Advanced Energy cells found on dissected packs)

evidence.quote: Once launched, the battery balance window turned red in the VTOL Control Window. The aircraft paused its launch and began to descend.
Upon reaching approximately 150 feet the aircraft stopped ascent and the vertical motors appeared to be struggling to continue its climb and transition.
Added to master ticket. HLB quarantined.
Battery Dissection led to discovery of leaking / evaporating electrolyte material inside the 3300mAh Advanced Energy Cells within the HLB.

team_view_in_comments: Added to master ticket. HLB quarantined.

would_settle_it.what: Per-cell HLB voltage plot from the launch showing which cell dropped
HLB cell voltages and balance status at the abort time
Cell impedance and dissection of the quarantined HLB to confirm the failed cell and mechanism

reasoning: The GCS battery balance window turned red right after launch and the aircraft then paused, descended and landed hard, which points directly at an HLB cell imbalance. The ticket was rolled into the systemic HLB cell failure investigation and the battery was quarantined. No per-cell data or teardown of this pack appears in the text, so the failed cell and the cell-level mechanism are not shown for this battery.
notes: The converted mishap form is a blank template with no incident data. Battery serial is inconsistent: a comment names battery 2-3490 from Kit 124, while the VXEP-1449 tracking table lists SN 4115 for VXE808 on 10-Jul-25 (and 3490 for VXE758). Master ticket VXEP-1449 root cause (electrolyte leaking/evaporating in Advanced Energy cells) is a fleet finding, not a teardown of this specific battery.

event: B35X battery charger SN 009 smoked and arced internally when plugged into a 35X main battery (SN 3L-0023), and smoked from under the circuit card on AC power; no aircraft involved.
component: B35X battery charger (P/N 2123091-01) BMS active balance board and PCA0120 DCDC board (U16)
failure_mode: Battery power shorted to battery ground through the cell balance lines and charger BMS balance board, damaging the cell 7 active balance board and U16 on PCA0120
contributing: Charger had earlier been connected to an incompatible SB30 FCR main battery, which is a known way to short it
Charger was red tagged before this use

evidence.quote: @Sean Wendling I believe this is the charger that a standard SB30 FCR main was accidently plugged into causing initial damage @Tom Westrich

Charger SN0009 was connected to a Main FCR battery, which has a known effect of shorting battery power to battery ground through the cell balance lines and the BMS balance board in the charger.  This unit was returned for repair and updates.
- Physical damage to active balancing board on cell 7
- Significant damage to U16 on PCA0120 (DCDC)

team_view_in_comments: I believe this is the charger that a standard SB30 FCR main was accidently plugged into causing initial damage
reasoning: The repair ticket BAT-78 states the charger had been connected to a Main FCR battery, which shorts battery power to ground through the balance lines and the charger BMS balance board. Inspection found a 13 ohm short across the main charge leads, a damaged cell 7 active balance board and a damaged U16 on PCA0120, matching the smoke and arcing reported. The boards were replaced, firmware updated to 1.2.32 and the unit passed testing.
notes: The incident ticket names a 35X main battery (SN 3L-0023) as the battery plugged in when it smoked; the damage is attributed to an earlier wrong-battery connection, so whether the smoke event itself was new damage or the earlier damage showing is not separated. Attachment CSV holds only calibration headers.

event: VXE-676 (TIQUILA, new aircraft on v6.3.4) showed a NAVIGATION ERROR MAGNETOMETER FAULT about 20 minutes into a night mission, then lost link for minutes, flew erratically in high winds and landed at the old landing zone after RTB.
component: magnetometer handling in VTOL AP and XCOMM software v6.3.4
failure_mode: Momentary invalid magnetometer samples not filtered out, setting the mag status bit invalid and raising the STANAG mag fault alert; known defect fixed in v6.4
contributing: Lost comms at about 8 km, cause not found (Silvus radio settings under review)
Erratic speed and heading attributed to gusty winds near the operating limit

reasoning: XCOMM and VTOL logs show the mag status going invalid twice for a moment while heading from FWAP and VTOL AP agreed, so the magnetometer itself performed well and the alert came from momentary bad samples. Engineers tie this to a known v6.3.4 defect where invalid mag data was not filtered, fixed in v6.4, and the release notes for v6.4 describe mag fault recovery fixes. The aircraft was on v6.3.4 awaiting approval of v6.4.

Others: lost comms (not determined, Silvus settings requested, possibly reduced power), erratic flight (attributed to winds near the limit), landing at the old PLZ (updated mission not received by the AP; GCS froze and was restarted), lost link behavior (LosRtbActiveLz=0 in last mission).
